<id>theme-zero-cpu-optimization</id> UI / Theming / Performance Zero-CPU Theme Optimization: Paint vs. Composite Lessons learned on achieving true zero-CPU runtime cost for UI themes, specifically for Firefox and XUL environments running on constrained hardware like Intel HD 4000. <lessons_learned> <lesson> Avoid CPU Paint Operations for Visual Feedback <detail>Changing properties like `outline`, `border`, `color`, or `background-color` triggers the CPU Paint stage (rasterizing elements to texture tiles). Instead, pre-bake outlines and borders using static CSS, and rely purely on `opacity` toggling to reveal or hide them.</detail> </lesson> <lesson> GPU Compositing via Opacity and Transform <detail>The only properties that can be fully offloaded to the GPU Compositor thread without waking the CPU are `opacity` and `transform`. The GPU's ROP (Raster Operations Pipeline) handles alpha blending natively.</detail> </lesson> <lesson> Hardware-Specific GPU Promotion (Intel HD 4000) <detail>To force fixed-function hardware (like Gen 7 Intel graphics) to promote a container to its own compositor layer, apply `transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0)` to the container and `will-change: opacity` to the interactive element BEFORE the interaction happens.</detail> </lesson> <lesson> Containment to Prevent Style Ripples <detail>Applying `contain: layout style` to major containers (like `#navigator-toolbox`) isolates style invalidations to that specific subtree, preventing calculations from cascading unnecessarily without breaking XUL flexbox contexts (unlike `contain: paint` which breaks layout).</detail> </lesson> <lesson> Minimize Z-Index Complexity <detail>Using aggressively high `z-index` values (like 2147483647) forces unnecessary new stacking contexts and compositor layers, wasting shared VRAM on integrated graphics. Use the absolute minimum `z-index` (e.g., `z-index: 2`) required to ensure clickability above other elements, specifically for elements like a hidden menubar.</detail> </lesson> <lesson> Fixing XUL Menubar and Ghost Text Buttons <detail>For unclickable text buttons injected over native XUL buttons: do not rely on pseudo-elements. Instead, set the native button to `display: -moz-box !important`, `min-width: 48px`, and `min-height: 24px` to ensure the click target perfectly overlaps the injected text. Avoid `position: relative` on menubars which causes flexbox collapse.</detail> </lesson> </lessons_learned> <related_scripts>
